# Cyanotic congenital heart defects

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Cardiology and angiology > Congenital heart diseases > Cyanotic congenital heart defects*

[Original Article Link](/library/Oo0IXS)

---

## Summary

<u>Cyanotic</u> <u>heart</u> defects (<u>CHDs</u>) are congenital cardiac <u>malformations</u> that commonly affect the atrial walls, e.g., the <u>right atrium</u> (<u>RA</u>) or <u>left atrium</u> (LA); ventricular walls, e.g., the <u>left ventricle</u> (LV) or <u>right ventricle</u> (RV); <u>heart valves</u>; or <u>large blood vessels</u>. Common causes include genetic defects (e.g., <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u>), maternal conditions (e.g., <u>diabetes</u>), and spontaneous genetic mutations. Pathophysiologically, <u>cyanotic</u> <u>heart</u> defects are characterized by a <u>right-to-left cardiac shunt</u>, which leads to deoxygenated blood entering the <u>systemic circulation</u>. The resulting <u>hypoxemia</u> manifests clinically as <u>cyanosis</u>, which may occur as acute, life-threatening episodes. Other symptoms include <u>failure to thrive</u>, characteristic <u>heart murmurs</u>, and <u>symptoms of heart failure</u>. Diagnosis is confirmed through visualization of the defect on <u>echocardiography</u>. Further diagnostic findings include low <u>oxygen saturation</u> and characteristic <u>x-ray</u> findings. <u>Heart</u> defects requiring treatment are repaired via catheter procedures or <u>surgery</u>. Supportive medical therapy is required in patients with <u>heart failure</u> (e.g., <u>diuretics</u>, <u>inotropic</u> agents) or if <u>surgery</u> cannot be performed (e.g., <u>prostaglandin</u>). If untreated, most <u>cyanotic</u> <u>heart</u> defects are fatal within the first year of life.

---

## Overview of cyanotic congenital heart defects

### Commonly associated conditions and risk factors of cyanotic congenital heart defects




|  | Most common associated conditions and <u>risk factors</u> |
| --- | --- |
| <u>Tetralogy of Fallot</u> | <br><br>* <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u><br><br>* <u>Down syndrome</u><br><br>* Maternal <u>risk factors</u><br><br>* <u>Alcohol</u> consumption<br><br>* <u>Phenylketonuria</u><br><br>* <u>Diabetes</u><br><br><br> |
| Transposition of great vessels | <br>* Maternal <u>risk factors</u>: <u>diabetes</u><br><br> |
| <u>Tricuspid valve atresia</u> | <br>* <u>Down syndrome</u><br><br> |
| <u>Ebstein anomaly</u> | <br>* Prenatal <u>lithium</u> exposure<br><br> |
| <u>Total anomalous pulmonary venous return</u> | <br>* <u>Heterotaxy syndromes</u><br><br> |
| <u>Persistent truncus arteriosus</u> | <br>* <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u><br><br> |
| <u>Hypoplastic left heart syndrome</u> | <br><br>* <u>Trisomy 13</u><br><br>* <u>Trisomy 18</u><br><br>* <u>Turner syndrome</u><br><br>* <u>Jacobsen syndrome</u><br><br><br> |





### General pathophysiological processes




* <u>CHDs</u> result from the disruption of the normal <u>cardiac morphogenesis</u> sequence.

* <u>CHDs</u> may lead to the formation of connections between the right and left <u>heart</u> (i.e., shunts).

* In <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHDs</u>: right-to-left cardiac shunting → blood flow from the right to the left <u>heart</u> → deoxygenated blood entering the <u>systemic circulation</u> → <u>cyanosis</u>





![Fetal and postnatal circulation](media/doyngxqk8ligke3xkgy6e35b.jpg)

Fetal and postnatal circulation




### General clinical features




* “Blue babies”: pale gray or blue <u>skin</u> color caused by <u>cyanosis</u>

* Feeding problems and <u>failure to thrive</u>

* <u>Exertional dyspnea</u>, <u>tachypnea</u>, and fatigue

* <u>Hypoxemia</u>  [[1]](/library/npb7Ju)[[2]](/library/LpbwJu)

* <u>Symptoms of heart failure</u> (see “<u>Acyanotic congenital heart defects</u>”)

* <u>Nail clubbing</u> may occur later in life.





> [!TIP]
> In approximately 50% of <u>infants</u> with <u>CHDs</u>, a routine <u>newborn</u> <u>physical examination</u> reveals no abnormalities. A normal <u>physical examination</u> does not rule out <u>CHD</u>. [[3]](/library/opb0qu)[[4]](/library/KpbUqu)




![Digital clubbing](media/can84kn62cgi6f4l0bc3p1f3.jpg)

Digital clubbing




### General treatment considerations [[5]](/library/lpbvpu)




* Ductal-dependent CHDs: a group of <u>CHDs</u> that require the <u>patent ductus arteriosus</u> (<u>PDA</u>), which supplies either pulmonary or <u>systemic circulation</u>, to sustain life until <u>surgery</u> can be performed [[6]](/library/kpbmpu)

* <u>PDA</u> supplies <u>systemic circulation</u> in the following:

* <u>Transposition of the great arteries</u>

* <u>Hypoplastic left heart syndrome</u>

* <u>Coarctation of the aorta</u>

* Critical <u>aortic valve stenosis</u>

* <u>PDA</u> supplies <u>pulmonary circulation</u> in the following:

* <u>Tricuspid atresia</u>

* Critical <u>pulmonary valve stenosis</u>, <u>tetralogy of Fallot</u>

* Treatment: administration of prostaglandin E1 infusion

* Example: IV <u>alprostadil</u> infusion (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)[[8]](/library/XJb9su)

* Mechanism of action: prevents the <u>ductus arteriosus</u> from closing, creating an intentional shunt to allow mixing of deoxygenated with oxygenated blood

* Monitor respiratory status and <u>hemodynamic parameters</u>.  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)

* In patients with <u>heart failure</u>  [[9]](/library/QrbuSE)

* Decrease fluid volume and lower <u>pulmonary vascular resistance</u> with <u>diuretics</u> or <u>ACE inhibitors</u>.

* Improve the contractility of the <u>heart</u> with <u>inotropic</u> agents (e.g., <u>digoxin</u>).

* <u>Antibiotic prophylaxis</u> for bacterial <u>endocarditis</u> during dental procedures [[10]](/library/XB09zR)[[11]](/library/Npb-pu)

* For all patients with unrepaired <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHDs</u>

* During the first six months after <u>surgery</u>

* Surgical repair is required in most cases.





> [!WARNING]
> Urgently consult critical care and pediatric cardiology for any <u>neonate</u> or <u>infant</u> presenting with <u>cyanosis</u> or <u>shock</u>. [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)




> [!NOTE]
> The “5 Ts” of <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHDs</u>: Tetralogy of Fallot, Transposition of the great vessels, Tricuspid valve anomalies, Total anomalous pulmonary <u>venous return</u>, and persistent Truncus arteriosus

---

## Tetralogy of Fallot

### Overview [[12]](/library/OrbIhE)




* Definition: <u>tetralogy of Fallot</u> (TOF) is the simultaneous occurrence of the following four defects:

* Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction (<u>RVOTO</u>) due to pulmonary infundibular stenosis

* <u>Right ventricular hypertrophy</u> (<u>RVH</u>)

* <u>Ventricular septal defect</u> (<u>VSD</u>)

* Overriding aorta (the aorta is displaced above the <u>VSD</u>)

* Other cardiac defects associated with TOF  [[13]](/library/IpbYIu)

* <u>Atrial septal defect</u> (<u>ASD</u>)

* <u>PDA</u>

* Anomalous <u>coronary arteries</u>  [[14]](/library/MHbMIE)





> [!NOTE]
> <u>RVOTO</u>: Right ventricular <u>hypertrophy</u>, Ventricular septal defect, Overriding aorta are the characteristics of Tetralogy of FallOt.





### <u>Epidemiology</u>




* <u>Prevalence</u>: 4–5/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[15]](/library/ppbLqu)

* The most common <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHD</u> [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)





### Etiology




* Typically sporadic [[17]](/library/8pbOru)

* Associated with the following genetic disorders:

* <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u> [[18]](/library/rpbfIu)[[19]](/library/7pb4Iu)

* <u>Down syndrome</u> [[20]](/library/HpbKIu)[[21]](/library/spbtIu)

* Maternal exposures during <u>pregnancy</u>

* <u>Alcohol</u> consumption

* <u>Phenylketonuria</u> [[22]](/library/GpbBIu)[[23]](/library/tpbXru)

* <u>Diabetes</u>  [[24]](/library/Fpbgru)[[25]](/library/FJbgDu)





### Pathophysiology




* During <u>fetal development</u>, <u>anterior</u> and superior deviation of the infundibular septum → misaligned <u>VSD</u> with overriding aortic root and subsequent <u>RVOTO</u>

* Physiologic blood flow is determined by the severity of <u>RVOTO</u>.

* A large <u>VSD</u> → equal pressures in the right and left ventricles → blood flow along the path of least resistance

* Severe <u>RVOTO</u> → flow from RV to LV → desaturated blood entering the circulation via the aorta





![Tetralogy of Fallot](media/uh84zitv93tjiy3e9o7sbbhe.jpg)

Tetralogy of Fallot




### Clinical findings




* <u>Infants</u> with mild TOF may be asymptomatic on initial examination.

* Mild to severe <u>cyanosis</u>, which depends on the severity of the <u>RVOTO</u>

* Mild obstruction → more pronounced <u>left-to-right shunt</u> via <u>VSD</u> → little or mild <u>cyanosis</u>

* Severe obstruction → more pronounced <u>right-to-left shunt</u> via <u>VSD</u> → severe <u>cyanosis</u>

* Tet spells: intermittent hypercyanotic, <u>hypoxic</u> episodes with a peak <u>incidence</u> at 2–4 months after <u>birth</u> ;   [[26]](/library/xvaEX5)[[27]](/library/AHbRGE)

* Associated with psychological and physical <u>stress</u> (e.g., crying, feeding, defecation)

* Caused by either an increase in <u>pulmonary vascular resistance</u> (<u>PVR</u>) or a decrease in <u>systemic vascular resistance</u> (<u>SVR</u>) → intermittent worsening of <u>RVOTO</u> and ↑ <u>right-to-left shunting</u>  [[28]](/library/ZJbZsu)[[29]](/library/0Jbesu)

* Spells occur suddenly and are potentially lethal.

* Untreated children tend to squat: squatting → ↑ <u>SVR</u> → ↓ <u>right-to-left shunt</u> → ↑ blood flow to <u>pulmonary circulation</u> → ↓ <u>hypoxemia</u> → relief of symptoms

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* Harsh <u>systolic ejection</u> <u>murmur</u> at the left upper sternal border

* Single <u>S2</u>

* Possible RV heave and systolic <u>thrill</u>

* <u>CHF</u> symptoms (see “Overview” in “<u>Heart failure</u>”)





> [!TIP]
> In patients with TOF, the <u>auscultated</u> <u>murmur</u> is determined by the amount of blood flow across the <u>RVOTO</u>. Therefore, during <u>tet spells</u>, the <u>murmur</u> may disappear.




![Tet spell in tetralogy of Fallot](media/uh3hqxcbf97pg1glt119bb4j.jpg)

Tet spell in tetralogy of Fallot




### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: Most cases are now diagnosed before <u>birth</u> due to improvements in fetal <u>echocardiography</u>. [[30]](/library/YJbnsu)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>) 

* Detection of the main features of TOF

* Quantification of <u>right ventricular</u> outflow tract pressure gradient

* Supplementary <u>cardiac catheterization</u> may be performed.

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>

* Boot-shaped heart (due to upturned cardiac apex and <u>RVH</u>)

* Normal or decreased <u>pulmonary vascular markings</u>

* <u>Concave</u> <u>pulmonary artery</u> segment

* <u>ECG</u>

* <u>Right axis deviation</u>

* Prominent <u>anterior</u> R waves (V1–V2)

* Prominent <u>posterior</u> S waves

* <u>Right atrial enlargement</u> and <u>RVH</u> (<u>P pulmonale</u>)

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>

* <u>Hyperoxia</u> test: helps to distinguish cardiac from pulmonary causes of <u>cyanosis</u>





![Tetralogy of Fallot](media/cex6v7ppo9uu5cbkthk6hg4h.jpg)

Tetralogy of Fallot

![Boot-shaped heart in tetralogy of Fallot](media/aanx5evp7rvov6epd1n9pgh5.jpg)

Boot-shaped heart in tetralogy of Fallot




### Treatment [[5]](/library/lpbvpu)[[31]](/library/cJbaGu)




* Severe <u>RVOTO</u>: <u>PGE1 infusion</u> until <u>surgery</u> [[8]](/library/XJb9su)

* Acute <u>hypoxia</u> (<u>tet spells</u>) ;  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0) [[32]](/library/cz1a7j0)

* Initial interventions

* Administer oxygen;  (e.g., 100% <u>FiO<sub>2</sub></u> via <u>NRB</u>).

* Knee to chest position, squatting

* IM <u>morphine</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)

* Subsequent interventions: Consider if no improvement.

* <u>IV sodium bicarbonate</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE to correct <u>metabolic acidosis</u>  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)

* <u>IV fluid resuscitation</u>

* <u>Vasopressors</u>, e.g., <u>phenylephrine</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)

* IV <u>beta blockers</u>, e.g., <u>propranolol</u> (<u>off label</u>) DOSAGE  [[7]](/library/AN1Rdh0)

* <u>Heart failure</u>

* <u>Inotropic</u> agents (e.g., <u>digoxin</u>) and <u>loop diuretics</u> (e.g., <u>furosemide</u>)

* <u>ACE inhibitors</u> are not recommended in patients with TOF because they may decrease <u>SVR</u> and promote <u>tet spells</u>.

* Surgical repair: performed within the first year of life ;  [[33]](/library/1Jb2Gu)[[34]](/library/WJbPGu)

* <u>VSD</u> repair: patch closure of the <u>ventricular septal defect</u> ensuring correct aortal positioning above the <u>left ventricle</u>

* Enlargement of the <u>RVOTO</u>: resection of the obstructive infundibular musculature

* If early surgical management is not possible: palliative shunts ;  [[35]](/library/dJboGu) [[36]](/library/VJbGGu)

* Blalock–Thomas–Taussig shunt: a palliative surgical procedure for TOF that connects the <u>subclavian artery</u> to the <u>pulmonary artery</u> with an interposed graft

* Central shunt

* Others (e.g., Potts shunt, Cooley shunt, Waterston shunt, Sano shunt)

* Follow-up care: to prevent long-term complications, such as <u>heart failure</u>, <u>arrhythmias</u> (e.g., <u>ventricular tachycardia</u>), and neurodevelopmental impairment





### Prognosis




* Without <u>surgery</u>, ∼ 50% of patients do not live past the first three years of life. [[37]](/library/67bj5E)

* With corrective <u>surgery</u>, over 90% of patients live to > 25 years of age. [[38]](/library/p7bL5E)

## Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)

### Overview




* Definition: anatomical reversal of the aorta and the <u>pulmonary artery</u>

* Other cardiac defects associated with <u>TGV</u> 

* <u>VSD</u>  [[39]](/library/krbmhE)

* <u>Left ventricular</u> <u>outlet obstruction</u>  [[40]](/library/UmXbUA)

* Abnormal valves and/or <u>coronary arteries</u>





### <u>Epidemiology</u>




* <u>Prevalence</u>: 2–4/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[15]](/library/ppbLqu)[[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)

* Accounts for ∼ 20% of all <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHD</u> cases  [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)





### Etiology




* Often multifactorial or unknown

* Intrauterine <u>risk factors</u>: <u>infants</u> born to mothers with <u>diabetes</u>  [[5]](/library/lpbvpu)[[24]](/library/Fpbgru)

* Genetic syndromes: seen in ∼ 1% of patients with <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u> [[41]](/library/KHbUrE)





### Pathophysiology [[42]](/library/vJbADu)




* Failed spiraling of the <u>aorticopulmonary septum</u> → RV emptying into the aorta and LV into the <u>pulmonary artery</u> → complete isolation of the pulmonary and systemic circuits → ↓ oxygenated blood entering the <u>systemic circulation</u>

* Fatal, unless mixing occurs via an intracardiac shunt (e.g., <u>PFO</u>, <u>VSD</u>, <u>ASD</u>) or via an extracardiac connection (e.g., <u>PDA</u>)





![Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)](media/lholhskee9xn324new6tlevx.jpg)

Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)

![Intracardiac shunt in the transposition of the great vessels](media/j4ibn4v57xxa7zn0sg4mnx00.jpg)

Intracardiac shunt in the transposition of the great vessels

![Ventricular septation](media/cva2prh5ysh35l55ykv16t8x.jpg)

Ventricular septation




### Clinical findings




* Postnatal <u>cyanosis</u> (not affected by exertion or <u>supplemental oxygen</u>)

* <u>Tachypnea</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* Single, loud <u>S2</u>

* There is often no <u>murmur</u>.

* Diminished femoral pulses

* If concurrent <u>VSD</u> is present: systolic <u>murmur</u> at the left sternal border





### Diagnostics [[5]](/library/lpbvpu)




* Prenatal diagnosis: <u>TGV</u> is difficult to diagnose with fetal <u>ultrasound</u>.  [[43]](/library/QsbuuE)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>)

* <u>Pulmonary artery</u> arising from the <u>left ventricle</u>

* Aorta arising from the <u>right ventricle</u>

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>

* “Egg on a string” appearance of the <u>heart</u>

* The enlarged, globular <u>heart</u> resembles an egg lying on its side.

* The string represents the <u>superior mediastinum</u> that appears narrow due to <u>stress</u>-induced <u>thymic</u> <u>atrophy</u>.

* ↑ Pulmonary vascular markings

* <u>MRI</u> (rarely done) showing the aorta arising from the <u>right ventricle</u> and the <u>pulmonary trunk</u> originating from the <u>left ventricle</u>

* <u>ECG</u>: often normal

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





![Transposition of the great vessels](media/fkk3j1olba5igm2b7mvk4290.jpg)

Transposition of the great vessels




### Treatment [[44]](/library/DJb1wu)




* Initial postnatal management: Initiate mixing between the two parallel circulations to ensure adequate systemic oxygenation.

* <u>Infusion of PGE1</u> to prevent closure of the <u>PDA</u> [[45]](/library/wJbhwu)

* Balloon atrial septostomy [[46]](/library/yJbd9u)[[47]](/library/AJbR9u)

* Objective: to enhance atrial mixing if <u>PGE1</u> administration is insufficient, and to alleviate <u>hypoxemia</u> [[48]](/library/_Jb59u)

* Procedure: <u>right heart catheterization</u> with the creation or enlargement of an existing <u>ASD</u>

* Surgical repair: recommended within the first two weeks of life  [[49]](/library/9JbNwu)[[50]](/library/CJbqwu)

* Arterial switch procedure: reversal of the aorta and <u>pulmonary artery</u> with insertion into the anatomically correct ventricle as well as correction of <u>coronary artery</u> supply  [[51]](/library/xJbEwu)[[52]](/library/BJbzwu)

* Rastelli procedure [[53]](/library/zJbr9u)[[54]](/library/-JbD9u)

* Indication: <u>TGV</u> with concurrent large <u>VSD</u> and <u>LVOTO</u> repair

* Procedure: creation of a conduit from the <u>LVOTO</u> through the <u>VSD</u> to the aorta  and creation of a conduit from the RV to the <u>pulmonary artery</u>





![Balloon atrial septostomy](media/ic6pi4gdielsmtd6arpibnqf.jpg)

Balloon atrial septostomy




### Prognosis




* Without treatment, 90% of patients with <u>TGA</u> die within the first year of life. [[55]](/library/2mXTUA)

* Long-term survival beyond 15–20 years of age is ∼ 90%. [[51]](/library/xJbEwu)

---

## Tricuspid valve atresia

### Overview




* Definition

* Absent or rudimentary <u>tricuspid valve</u> resulting in no blood flow between the <u>RA</u> and the RV

* Patient survival is only possible if there are interatrial and interventricular communications (see “Other cardiac defects” below).  [[56]](/library/Xsb9tE)

* Other cardiac defects associated with <u>tricuspid valve atresia</u>

* <u>ASD</u>

* <u>VSD</u>

* RV <u>hypoplasia</u>

* Other defects (e.g., pulmonary outflow obstruction, <u>aortic stenosis</u>, <u>aortic coarctation</u>)





### <u>Epidemiology</u>




* <u>Prevalence</u>: 0.2–1.2/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)

* Third most common <u>cyanotic</u> <u>CHD</u>





### Pathophysiology




* <u>Tricuspid atresia</u> is accompanied by RV <u>hypoplasia</u> and <u>RA</u> dilation due to <u>volume overload</u> (univentricular <u>heart</u>).

* Circulation depends on the presence of interatrial and interventricular communications.

* Blood in the <u>RA</u> flows through the <u>ASD</u> into the LA → venous blood mixes with arterial blood in the left <u>heart</u> → <u>cyanosis</u>

* Blood can only reach the RV and pulmonary system via a <u>VSD</u>.





![Tricuspid valve atresia](media/f2ncls7kpd9j7itwn3bairyp.jpg)

Tricuspid valve atresia




### Clinical features




* <u>Central cyanosis</u> (occurs within days after <u>birth</u>)

* <u>Tachypnea</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* <u>Holosystolic murmur</u> at the lower left sternal border

* Single <u>S2</u>

* <u>Jugular venous distention</u> with a prominent <u>A wave</u>

* Diminished peripheral pulses





### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: fetal <u>echocardiography</u> at 18–22 weeks' <u>gestation</u> [[57]](/library/LsbwvE)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>)

* Absent <u>tricuspid valve</u>

* <u>ASD</u>

* RV <u>hypoplasia</u>

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>

* Mild <u>cardiomegaly</u>

* Abnormal <u>pulmonary markings</u>

* <u>ECG</u> [[58]](/library/MsbMvE)

* <u>LVH</u> with <u>left axis deviation</u>

* Tall <u>P waves</u>

* Minimal R waves in <u>precordial leads</u>

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





### Treatment




* Initial postnatal management: cardiopulmonary stabilization until surgical <u>palliation</u>

* <u>PGE1 infusion</u>

* Cardiorespiratory support (e.g., <u>inotropes</u>, <u>mechanical ventilation</u>, <u>supplemental oxygen</u>)

* Surgical repair: three-stage surgical <u>palliation</u> to isolate both pulmonary and systemic circulations (see “Surgical repair” in “<u>Hypoplastic left heart syndrome</u>”)

* Optional temporary measures

* In cases with concurrent <u>pulmonary valve</u> <u>atresia</u> or severe stenosis: systemic-to-pulmonary shunt (<u>Blalock-Taussig shunt</u>) to improve <u>perfusion</u>

* Risk of <u>pulmonary hypertension</u>: <u>pulmonary artery</u> <u>banding</u> to control pulmonary hyperperfusion





### Prognosis



* With <u>surgery</u>, ∼ 90% of patients live to the age of one year and the 10-year survival rate is ∼ 80%. [[56]](/library/Xsb9tE)

---

## Ebstein anomaly

### Overview




* Definition: malformed <u>tricuspid valve</u> leaflets that are displaced into the <u>right ventricle</u> with subsequent <u>tricuspid valve regurgitation</u> and right <u>heart</u> enlargement (known as RV “atrialization”)

* Other cardiac defects associated with <u>Ebstein anomaly</u>

* Interatrial communication (e.g., <u>PFO</u>, <u>ASD</u>): seen in ∼ 90% of patients [[59]](/library/aB0QzR)

* Conduction disorders (e.g., <u>Wolff-Parkinson-White</u> syndrome, <u>supraventricular tachycardia</u>) [[60]](/library/nHb7IE)





### <u>Epidemiology</u>




* <u>Prevalence</u>: 0.5–1/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[61]](/library/lrbvhE)

* Accounts for < 1% of all <u>CHD</u> cases [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)





### Etiology




* Multifactorial (most cases are sporadic) [[62]](/library/Nrb-hE)

* Associated with prenatal <u>lithium</u> exposure  [[63]](/library/mrbV3E)[[64]](/library/5rbi3E)

* Isolated genetic defects (e.g., <u>MYH7</u> which encodes β-<u>myosin</u> <u>heavy chain</u>)





### Pathophysiology [[59]](/library/aB0QzR)



* Incomplete delamination (i.e., separation of valve tissue from the <u>myocardium</u>) during valve development can lead to one or more of the following: 

* Incomplete closure of the <u>right atrioventricular valve</u> and reduction in RV volume → tricuspid regurgitation→ <u>RA</u> dilation → <u>right heart failure</u>

* <u>RV atrialization</u> → reduced function of the RV → insufficient systolic contraction → functional <u>pulmonary valve</u> <u>atresia</u> → ↓ pulmonary flow → ↓ <u>cardiac output</u> → systemic <u>hypoperfusion</u>, <u>dyspnea</u>, and fatigue

* Bulging of the large sail-like <u>anterior</u> tricuspid leaflet into the RV → <u>RVOTO</u> → ↑ right <u>heart</u> pressure → ↑ flow through the <u>patent foramen ovale</u> → <u>right-to-left shunt</u> → <u>cyanosis</u>




![Ebstein anomaly](media/f69k9u5u8ggczgd6crw6ldgi.jpg)

Ebstein anomaly

![Ebstein anomaly](media/fncqkwvl24kszi89s3f9w9zv.jpg)

Ebstein anomaly




### Clinical findings [[59]](/library/aB0QzR)




* The clinical presentation of <u>Ebstein anomaly</u> varies according to the severity of the abnormality. [[65]](/library/oHb0rE)

* Mild apical displacement → asymptomatic presentation throughout adulthood

* Moderate tricuspid leaflet displacement → <u>cyanosis</u> or <u>heart failure</u> in <u>infancy</u> or childhood

* Severe displacement → in utero <u>heart</u> failure → nonimmune <u>hydrops fetalis</u> → <u>death</u>

* <u>Neonates</u> and children

* <u>Cyanosis</u>

* Severe <u>cardiomegaly</u> and <u>heart failure</u>

* <u>Respiratory distress</u>

* <u>Adolescents</u> and adults

* <u>Arrhythmias</u> e.g., <u>Wolff-Parkinson-White</u> syndrome

* <u>Exertional dyspnea</u> and fatigue

* <u>Palpitations</u> and <u>sudden cardiac death</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* <u>Loud S1</u>

* Widely <u>split S1</u> and <u>S2</u>

* <u>Holosystolic murmur</u> at the left sternal border





### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: fetal <u>echocardiography</u>

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>)

* Enlarged right <u>heart</u>

* <u>Tricuspid regurgitation</u>

* <u>Chest x-ray</u> 

* Mild to severe <u>cardiomegaly</u>

* <u>RA enlargement</u>

* <u>MRI</u> : apical displacement of the septal and <u>posterior</u> tricuspid leaflets

* <u>ECG</u>

* Tall and broad <u>P waves</u>

* <u>First-degree atrioventricular block</u>

* <u>Right axis deviation</u>

* <u>Right bundle branch block</u>

* Findings specific for <u>WPW</u> syndrome (e.g., delta wave)

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





![Cardiomegaly in Ebstein anomaly](media/um1mwn8rguffh87c43cvodr0.jpg)

Cardiomegaly in Ebstein anomaly




### Treatment




* Initial postnatal management: stabilization of cardiorespiratory status until <u>PVR</u> decreases and <u>surgery</u> can be performed

* <u>PGE1 infusion</u>

* <u>Inhaled nitric oxide</u> or infusion of <u>milrinone</u>

* Surgical repair

* Objective: creation of a systemic-pulmonary shunt, repair of the <u>tricuspid valve</u>, and reconstruction of the <u>right ventricle</u>

* Age-related considerations

* <u>Neonates</u> and <u>infants</u>: should be avoided in <u>infancy</u> and delayed as long as possible  [[66]](/library/JHbsrE)

* Children and adults: recommended if concomitant <u>heart failure</u> or progressive RV dysfunction is present [[67]](/library/pHbLrE)

* <u>Arrhythmias</u>: <u>catheter ablation</u> of the aberrant pathway [[68]](/library/qHbCrE)





### Prognosis




* Varies according to the severity of disease

* Around 30% of patients die within the first year of life. [[65]](/library/oHb0rE)

---

## Total anomalous pulmonary venous return (TAPVR)

### Overview




* Definition: All four <u>pulmonary veins</u> drain into the systemic venous circulation (e.g., <u>SVC</u>, <u>sinus venosus</u>, <u>RA</u>, <u>IVC</u>) instead of the <u>left atrium</u>.

* Other cardiac defects associated with <u>TAPVR</u>: allow for <u>right-to-left shunting</u> and the mixing of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood

* <u>ASD</u>

* <u>PDA</u>





![Total anomalous pulmonary venous return](media/z53e5erptx585cl25m1zfq1g.jpg)

Total anomalous pulmonary venous return




### <u>Epidemiology</u>



* <u>Prevalence</u>: 0.6–1.2/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)




### Etiology




* Multifactorial (may be associated with genetic alterations) [[69]](/library/-sbDxE)

* Associated with <u>heterotaxy syndromes</u> that involve <u>asplenia</u> [[70]](/library/ZGbZBE)[[71]](/library/0GbeBE)





### Pathophysiology




The severity of symptoms and clinical presentation is determined by the following factors:




* Venous mixing: oxygenated pulmonary <u>venous return</u> mixes with the systemic venous system →  <u>right-to-left shunting</u> of partially oxygenated blood via an interatrial connection (e.g., <u>ASD</u>, <u>PFO</u>, rarely <u>PDA</u>) into the systemic arterial circulation → <u>cyanosis</u>

* Pulmonary venous obstruction: obstruction of pulmonary venous return → ↑ pulmonary venous pressure → ↑ <u>pulmonary edema</u> → ↑ <u>PVR</u> → <u>RVH</u>, ventricular dilation, and <u>heart failure</u>





### Clinical features [[72]](/library/aGbQBE)




* <u>Cyanosis</u>

* <u>Respiratory failure</u>

* Poor feeding and <u>failure to thrive</u>

* <u>Hepatomegaly</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings 

* <u>Fixed split</u> <u>S2</u>;   or loud <u>S2</u>

* <u>Systolic ejection</u> <u>murmur</u> with <u>diastolic</u> rumble  or mild to no <u>murmur</u>





### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: fetal <u>echocardiography</u> to detect abnormal pulmonary <u>venous return</u> [[73]](/library/dGboyE)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>)

* Malposition of <u>pulmonary veins</u>

* Enlarged right <u>heart</u>

* Right-to-left interatrial shunting

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>

* “Snowman sign” (seen in supracardiac <u>TAPVR</u>): the orientation of the <u>heart</u> and <u>superior mediastinum</u> appear as the shape of a snowman

* Pulmonary hypervascularity

* Right <u>heart</u> enlargement

* <u>ECG</u> [[72]](/library/aGbQBE)

* Nonspecific findings

* <u>Right axis deviation</u> due to <u>RVH</u>

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





### Treatment




* Initial postnatal management: stabilization of cardiorespiratory status until <u>surgery</u> is performed (e.g., <u>mechanical ventilation</u>, <u>supplemental O<sub>2</sub></u>, <u>inotropes</u>)

* Surgical repair: recommended in all patients regardless of the severity of disease [[74]](/library/bGbHBE)





### Prognosis




* With surgical correction, the long-term survival rate is 80–90%. [[75]](/library/XGb9BE)

* Without treatment, ∼ 80% of patients die within the first year of life. [[76]](/library/cGbayE)

---

## Persistent truncus arteriosus

### Overview




* Definition: underdevelopment of the <u>aorticopulmonary septum</u> → failure of the <u>truncus arteriosus</u> to divide into the aorta and <u>pulmonary trunk</u> → a single trunk that receives output from both ventricles

* Other cardiac defects associated with <u>persistent truncus arteriosus</u>

* <u>VSD</u>

* Interrupted <u>aortic arch</u> [[77]](/library/lsbvEE)

* <u>Coronary artery</u> anomalies [[78]](/library/RrblSE)





### <u>Epidemiology</u>



* <u>Prevalence</u>: ∼ 1/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)




### Etiology




* The failure of <u>neural crest cells</u> to migrate during the development of the cardiac outflow tract results in incomplete <u>AP septum</u> formation. [[79]](/library/HIbKVE)

* Associated with <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u> [[80]](/library/sIbtVE)[[81]](/library/GIbBVE)





### Pathophysiology




* Deoxygenated and oxygenated blood mix via the <u>VSD</u> → the <u>truncus arteriosus</u> receiving both RV and LV output → blood flow to both pulmonary and systemic circulations

* The severity of disease is determined by <u>pulmonary vascular resistance</u> (<u>PVR</u>).





### Clinical features




* <u>Cyanosis</u>

* <u>Respiratory distress</u>

* <u>Failure to thrive</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* Bounding peripheral pulses

* Harsh systolic <u>murmur</u> at the lower left sternal border

* Loud <u>S2</u>





### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: fetal <u>echocardiography</u>  [[82]](/library/Nsb-EE)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>): single overriding great vessel arising from the <u>heart</u>

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>

* Right-sided <u>aortic arch</u>

* ↑ Pulmonary vascular markings

* Absent <u>thymus</u>, if associated with <u>DiGeorge syndrome</u>

* <u>ECG</u>: often normal and nonspecific findings

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





### Treatment




* Initial medical management: stabilization of cardiopulmonary function (e.g., <u>diuretics</u>, <u>dopamine</u>, ventilation, correction of <u>metabolic acidosis</u>) [[9]](/library/QrbuSE)

* Surgical repair: Surgical correction is recommended in the <u>neonatal period</u>. [[83]](/library/PrbWhE)[[84]](/library/4rb3hE)





### Prognosis



* With surgical repair, the 30-year survival rate is ∼ 70%. [[85]](/library/5sbivE)




![Persistent truncus arteriosus](media/p100wqptfwz99me3b1822e4p.jpg)

Persistent truncus arteriosus

## Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS)

### Overview



* Definition: spectrum of disease consisting of severe <u>hypoplasia</u> of the <u>left ventricle</u> with possible stenosis and/or <u>atresia</u> of the <u>mitral valve</u>, <u>aortic valve</u>, or <u>aortic arch</u> [[86]](/library/OIbI1E)




### <u>Epidemiology</u>




* Extremely rare (2–3/10,000 <u>live births</u> in the US [[16]](/library/Jpbsqu)[[87]](/library/lIbv1E)

* Sex: <u>♂</u> > <u>♀</u> (1.5:1) [[88]](/library/NIb-1E)

* Although rare, <u>HLHS</u> is responsible for 25–40% of all neonatal cardiac deaths. [[89]](/library/TmX6UA)





### Etiology




* Multifactorial: associated with single <u>gene</u> <u>polymorphisms</u>, altered blood flow patterns, and intrauterine infection [[90]](/library/5IbiWE)[[91]](/library/MIbMWE)[[92]](/library/nIb7WE)

* Syndromic associations: <u>trisomy 13</u>, <u>trisomy 18</u>, <u>Jacobsen syndrome</u>, and <u>Turner syndrome</u> [[93]](/library/mIbVWE)[[94]](/library/LIbwWE)





### Pathophysiology




* The <u>hypoplastic left ventricle</u> is nonfunctional, resulting in the RV becoming the primary supply for pulmonary and systemic circulations.

* Survival depends on the presence of a <u>PDA</u> (<u>right-to-left shunt</u>);   and an <u>ASD</u>.





![Cyanotic congenital heart defects: hypoplastic left heart syndrome](media/iq18c1mdjuq9lal1qxpvt7cw.jpg)

Cyanotic congenital heart defects: hypoplastic left heart syndrome




### Clinical findings




* May be asymptomatic at <u>birth</u> if the open <u>PDA</u> provides adequate systemic <u>perfusion</u>

* Aggravation of symptoms following closure of the <u>PDA</u>

* Postnatal <u>cyanosis</u> (not corrected by supplement O<sub>2</sub>)

* <u>Tachypnea</u>

* ↓ BP, ↓ peripheral pulses, and cool extremities

* <u>Heart failure</u> and <u>cardiogenic shock</u>

* <u>Cardiac examination</u> findings

* Typically no <u>murmur</u>

* Loud, single <u>S2</u>





### Diagnostics




* Prenatal diagnosis: fetal <u>echocardiography</u>  [[95]](/library/6HbjrE)

* Imaging

* <u>Echocardiography</u> (<u>confirmatory test</u>): visualization of absent or <u>hypoplastic</u> LV

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>: variable and nonspecific findings

* <u>ECG</u>: typically normal

* <u>Pulse oximetry</u>: ↓ <u>SpO<sub>2</sub></u>





### Treatment




* Initial medical management: continuous <u>PGE1 infusion</u> prior to <u>heart</u> <u>surgery</u>  [[96]](/library/JIbsdE)

* Surgical repair: Palliative <u>surgery</u> is used in single-ventricular cardiopathologies. [[88]](/library/NIb-1E)

* Three-step staged surgical correction 

* Norwood procedure (stage I): performed while the patient is a <u>neonate</u> [[97]](/library/KIbUdE)[[98]](/library/IIbYVE)

* Glenn procedure (stage II): performed at ∼ 3–6 months of age [[99]](/library/rIbfVE)

* <u>Fontan procedure</u> (stage III): performed after 2–3 years of age [[100]](/library/7Ib4VE)

* Alternative: <u>heart transplant</u>  [[101]](/library/qIbCdE)





### Prognosis




* Even with surgical correction, the 5-year survival rate remains low (∼ 65%). [[97]](/library/KIbUdE)

* For patients that survive to one year of age, long-term survival (up to 18 years of age) is ∼ 90%. [[102]](/library/6IbjdE)[[103]](/library/pIbLdE)
